title: The small "i" on a set that explains its target is hard to hit
what: When a set has a reason behind its target, a tiny round "i" is drawn on the corner of the set number. It is 14 points wide and its touch area reaches only about 30 points, and it sits on top of the set number, which opens the set type choices. A finger often opens the wrong thing.
expected: The "why" mark can be tapped on its own with a normal finger, at least 48 points, without landing on the set number.
how_often: every set that shows the mark
fix_line: Make the why mark larger or move it beside the set number so its touch area is full finger size

title: A screen reader skips the explaining line under some workout settings
what: In workout settings, rows such as Default rest, Rest-over sound, Weight step and Reps to aim for read out only their name and value. The small line under each one is never read, including "Workout sounds are off: Rest is over only buzzes" and "Change it per exercise from the exercise's menu".
expected: A screen reader user hears the same explanation a sighted member reads under each setting.
fix_line: Add the explaining line to what the screen reader says for these rows, or as a hint

title: The minimised workout bar does not say the rest time left or the workout time
what: The bar above the tabs shows the rest countdown or the time trained in large numbers. A screen reader only hears "Rest, 3 sets done, tap to open the workout", never how many seconds of rest are left or how long the workout has run.
expected: The bar reads out the same time it shows, for example "Rest, 45 seconds left".
how_often: every time a workout is minimised
fix_line: Put the shown time into what the screen reader says for the bar

title: "Not now" on the watch install card looks like plain grey words
what: On the one-time "Install MettleUp on your watch" card at the start of a workout, "Not now" is grey text with no outline or underline, next to the orange "Install on watch". It does not look like something to tap.
expected: Every choice on the card looks tappable.
how_often: once, the first workout with a watch
fix_line: Give Not now a button look, such as an outline or the same colour style as the other choice

title: The "older names" fold in the routine import does not say if it is open
what: When bringing routines in after a Hevy or Strong import, the row "N older names (not used for a year)" opens a hidden list. A screen reader is not told whether it is open or closed, and its arrow always points right, even when open.
expected: The screen reader says open or closed, and the arrow turns when the list is open.
who: members switching from Hevy or Strong
fix_line: Mark the row as open or closed for the screen reader and turn the arrow
